evidence.text: GENERAL MAINTENANCE In extremely dusty locations, dirt may clog the air passages causing the welder to run hot. Blow dirt out of the welder with low-pressure air at regular intervals to eliminate excessive dirt and dust build-up on internal parts.

nodes.name: Cable liner

properties.name: Cable liner
properties.description: Cable liner

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

properties.description: Circuit breaker

evidence.text: column 1: No wire feed, weld output or gas flow when gun trigger is pulled. Fan does NOT operate. | column 2: 1. Make sure correct voltage is applied to the machine. 2. Make certain that power switch is in the ON position. 3. Make sure circuit breaker is reset. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

nodes.name: Power switch

properties.name: Power switch
properties.description: Power switch

evidence.text: column 1: No wire feed, weld output or gas flow when gun trigger is pulled. Fan does NOT operate. | column 2: 1. Make sure correct voltage is applied to the machine. 2. Make certain that power switch is in the ON position. 3. Make sure circuit breaker is reset. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

nodes.name: Spool gun switch

properties.name: Spool gun switch
properties.description: Spool gun switch

evidence.text: column 1: No wire feed when gun trigger is pulled. Fan runs, gas flows and machine has correct open circuit volt- age (33V) - weld output. | column 2: 1. If the wire drive motor is running make sure that the correct drive rolls are installed in the machine. 2. Check for clogged cable liner or con- tact tip. 3. Check for proper size cable liner and contact tip. 4. Check if the spool gun switch, locat- ed in the wire drive compartment, is set to the desired location. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

Gun trigger may be faulty. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

nodes.name: Wire drive mechanism

properties.name: Wire drive mechanism
properties.description: Wire drive mechanism

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

evidence.text: column 1: Major physical or electrical damage is evident. | column 2: “Do not Plug in machine or turn it on.” Contact your local Authorized Field Service Facility. | column 3: If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

column 1: No wire feed, weld output or gas flow when gun trigger is pulled. Fan does NOT operate. | column 2: 1. Make sure correct voltage is applied to the machine. 2. Make certain that power switch is in the ON position. 3. Make sure circuit breaker is reset. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

column 1: No wire feed, weld output or gas flow when gun trigger is pulled. Fan oper- ates normally. | column 2: 1. The thermostat may be tripped due to overheating. Let machine cool. Weld at lower duty cycle. 2. Check for obstructions in air flow. Check Gun Trigger connections. See installation section. 3. Gun trigger may be faulty. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

column 1: No wire feed when gun trigger is pulled. Fan runs, gas flows and machine has correct open circuit volt- age (33V) - weld output. | column 2: 1. If the wire drive motor is running make sure that the correct drive rolls are installed in the machine. 2. Check for clogged cable liner or con- tact tip. 3. Check for proper size cable liner and contact tip. 4. Check if the spool gun switch, locat- ed in the wire drive compartment, is set to the desired location. | column 3 (same as row above): If all recommended possible areas of mis- adjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

column 1: Error Code 003,010,013 Is displayed on screen | column 2: 1. Communication error between display P.C. board and power control board. | column 3: 1. Cycle power to machine 2. Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

properties.name: Dirt in the cable liner
properties.description: Dirt in the cable liner

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

nodes.name: Arc is unstable and starting is poor

properties.name: Arc is unstable and starting is poor
properties.description: Arc is unstable and starting is poor

evidence.text: column 1: Arc is unstable - Poor starting. | column 2: 1. Check for correct input voltage to machine. 2. Check for proper electrode polarity for process. 3. Check gun tip for wear or damage and proper size - Replace. 4. Check for proper gas and flow rate for process. (For MIG only.) 5. Check work cable for loose or faulty connections. 6. Check gun for damage or breaks. 7. Check for proper drive roll ori- entation and alignment. 8. Check liner for proper size. | column 3: If all recommended possible areas of misadjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

Use only partial air pressure; excessive pressure at the beginning of cable-liner cleaning may form a dirt plug.

evidence.text: Have qualified personnel do all maintenance and troubleshooting work.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: Have qualified personnel do all maintenance and troubleshooting work.

To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.
Before carrying out service, maintenance and/or repair jobs, fully disconnect power to the machine.

conditions.text: After using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode.
Fully disconnect power before carrying out service, maintenance, or repair work.
Have qualified personnel perform all maintenance and troubleshooting work.
Use PPE, including safety glasses, dust mask, and gloves; this also applies to persons entering the work area.
Moving parts can injure: do not operate with doors open or guards off; stop the engine before servicing; keep away from moving parts.

notes: one end is not named in the source

evidence.text: Have qualified personnel do all maintenance and troubleshooting work.

To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.
Before carrying out service, maintenance and/or repair jobs, fully disconnect power to the machine.
Use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, dust mask and gloves to avoid injury. This also applies to persons who enter the work area.
MOVING PARTS can injure. • Do not operate with doors open or guards off. • Stop engine before servicing. • Keep away from moving parts.

conditions.text: Before service, maintenance, or repair work, fully disconnect power to the machine.
Have qualified personnel perform maintenance and troubleshooting.
Remove the cable from the wire feeder, lay it straight on the floor, and remove the contact tip from the gun
Use PPE, including safety glasses, a dust mask, and gloves.
Do not operate with doors open or guards off; stop the engine before servicing; keep away from moving parts.
Use only partial air pressure; excessive pressure at the beginning may cause dirt to form a plug

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

Have qualified personnel perform all maintenance and troubleshooting work.
Use only partial air pressure; excessive pressure at the beginning of cable-liner cleaning may form a dirt plug.
